newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-ITALIAN SERIE A MATCHES ON SUNDAY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ITALIAN SERIE A MATCHES ON SUNDAY.

text.p: Italian serie A games due to be played on Sunday (kick-off times GMT):

Bologna will be without Swedish striker Kennet Andersson, controversially sent off against Vicenza last Sunday, for this difficult derby. In-form Parma, winners against Milan and Juventus on their last two outings, will be without suspended strikers Enrico Chiesa and Alessandro Melli as well as Argentines Nestor Sensini and Hernan Crespo, on international duty.

League leaders Juventus will be without French midfielder Zinedine Zidane and defender Moreno Torricelli, both suspended, but field a strong attack of Alessandro Del Piero, Croat Alen Boksic and Michele Padovano. Atlanta, unbeaten in five games, rely on an attack of Gigi Lentini and Filippo Inzaghi, the league's leading goalscorer with 11.

Can the revelation side of the season, Vicenza, take another noble scalp? Vicenza are at almost full strength while Milan are without Liberian striker George Weah, French striker Christophe Dugarry and defender Paolo Maldini, all injured, and team morale is at rock bottom following consecutive defeats by Parma and Lazio.

An important test for Inter who will be without suspended Englishman Paul Ince, Chilean striker Ivan Zamorano, on international duty, and the injured Nicola Berti. Napoli, beaten 3-0 last week by Fiorentina, rely on Brazilians Beto and Cruz and Frenchman Alain Boghossian in midfield.

A relegation battle between two sides both on 17 points. Pasquale Luiso leads the Piacenza attack while Udinese will be without four injured foreigners -- German striker Oliver Bierhoff, Egyptian midfielder Hazem Emam, Polish defender Marek Kozminski and Danish defender Thomas Helveg.
Fiorentina will be without influential captain Gabriel Batistuta, on international call-up, but should still prove too strong for bottom side Reggiana.

Former Parma coach Nevio Scala is unlikely to ring many changes for his first game since taking over from Giovanni Galeone at Perugia. Inconsistent Roma, beaten by Atalanta and Inter in their last two outings, look to Argentine striker Abel Balbo.

Arguably the most in-form Italian side of the moment, Sampdoria should have too much firepower for relegation battlers Cagliari. Roberto Mancini, Argentine Juan Veron, Frenchmen Pierre Laigle and Christian Karembeu all feature for the home side while Cagliari look to the experienced Sandro Tovalieri in attack.

Boosted by a 3-0 win against Milan last week, Lazio will fancy their chances against second-from-bottom Verona. Giuseppe Signori, Roberto Rambaudi and Pierluigi Casiraghi form the Lazio attack while Verona rely on Filippo Maniero in attack and Raffaele Ametrano in midfield.
